<b>Основание черепа изнутри</b>, свод сн: The base of the skull from inside, with the vault removed. The nerves leave the skull through openings in its three cranial fossae: anterior (I), middle (II–VI), and posterior (VII–XII). Where several nerves share one opening, disease at that spot affects them together. Choose a nerve.
<b>I — решётчатая пластинка.</b> Около 2: I — the cribriform plate. About 20 olfactory filaments pass from the nose through the holes of the ethmoid bone to the olfactory bulb. A fracture of the skull base tears them — the sense of smell is lost, and cerebrospinal fluid may leak from the nose.
<b>II — зрительный канал</b> в малом кры: II — the optic canal in the lesser wing of the sphenoid bone; the ophthalmic artery runs through it together with the nerve. Just behind the canal the nerves meet at the chiasm above the sella turcica — a pituitary tumor pressing on it from below causes loss of the outer (temporal) visual fields.
<b>III — верхняя глазничная щель.</b> Не: III — the superior orbital fissure. The nerve runs in the wall of the cavernous sinus and enters the orbit through the fissure. Nerves IV and VI and the ophthalmic nerve V₁ pass through the same fissure, so damage there disables almost all eye movements.
<b>IV — верхняя глазничная щель.</b> Сам: IV — the superior orbital fissure. The thinnest nerve with the longest path inside the skull: it winds around the brainstem, runs in the wall of the cavernous sinus, and enters the orbit to reach the superior oblique muscle.
<b>V — три ветви, три отверстия.</b> Гла: V — three branches, three openings. The ophthalmic nerve V₁ leaves through the superior orbital fissure, the maxillary V₂ through the foramen rotundum, and the mandibular V₃ through the foramen ovale. The trigeminal ganglion sits in a depression at the apex of the petrous temporal bone.
<b>VI — верхняя глазничная щель.</b> Нер: VI — the superior orbital fissure. The nerve climbs the clivus, bends over the apex of the petrous bone, and passes through the cavernous sinus next to the carotid artery. Because of its long path it is often affected when intracranial pressure rises.
<b>VII — внутренний слуховой проход.</b>: VII — the internal acoustic meatus. The facial nerve enters it together with VIII, runs in a narrow bony canal through the temporal bone, and leaves the skull through the stylomastoid foramen. Swelling of the nerve in this tight canal causes Bell palsy.
<b>VIII — внутренний слуховой проход.</b: VIII — the internal acoustic meatus. Its path is short: from the meatus the nerve goes straight into the inner ear in the petrous temporal bone. A tumor of its sheath (vestibular schwannoma) grows in the meatus and causes one-sided hearing loss and ringing in the ear.
<b>IX — яремное отверстие.</b> Через нег: IX — the jugular foramen. Nerves IX, X, and XI share it with venous blood from the sigmoid sinus, which becomes the internal jugular vein here. A tumor at this spot affects all three nerves at once: swallowing, voice, and head turning suffer.
<b>X — яремное отверстие.</b> Блуждающий: X — the jugular foramen. The vagus nerve leaves the skull together with IX and XI and descends the neck beside the carotid artery and jugular vein to the organs of the chest and abdomen.
<b>XI — путь туда и обратно.</b> Корешки: XI — there and back. The roots of the accessory nerve start in the cervical spinal cord, rise into the skull through the foramen magnum, and leave again through the jugular foramen — to the trapezius and sternocleidomastoid muscles.
<b>XII — подъязычный канал</b> над мыщел: XII — the hypoglossal canal above the occipital condyle, at the front edge of the foramen magnum. The nerve goes to the tongue muscles; when it is damaged, the protruded tongue deviates toward the affected side.
\n <div><h2>Как их запомнить</h2>\n:
How to remember them

Sensory: I, II, VIII: smell, vision, the inner ear (hearing and balance). Motor: IV, VI, XI, XII. Motor with parasympathetic fibers: III (constricts the pupil). Mixed: V, VII, IX, X: in their set of functions they are closest to spinal nerves; parasympathetic fibers also run in VII, IX and X.

Where they emerge

I enters the telencephalon, II the diencephalon. III and IV emerge from the midbrain (IV is the only one on the dorsal side). V is associated with the pons. VI, VII and VIII emerge at the border of the pons and the medulla, IX–XII from the medulla.

Evolution

The set did not appear all at once: fish and amphibians have no separate XI and XII nerves (their fibers run within the vagus and spinal nerves), and the full set of 12 pairs is found in amniotes: reptiles, birds and mammals. The medulla and pons retain the plan of the spinal cord: sensory nuclei lie laterally, motor nuclei medially, and parasympathetic nuclei between them.

What is accurate here

  • Where the nerves emerge on the underside of the brain.
  • Classification by function and the direction of the signal.
  • The ganglion and three branches of the trigeminal nerve.
  • The openings in the base of the skull and the nerves that pass through them (mode 2, a scan of a real skull).

  • The targets (eye, ear, tongue, heart) are moved close to the brain and drawn as icons.
  • The course of the nerves inside the skull is simplified.
  • In the Skull openings mode, the positions of the openings on the scan are approximate, and the nerves are shown as short segments.
